reviewer: Claude (Opus 5) review agent, independent of the extractor; no human review claimed
scope: Independent review of the GPN-MSA published-version batch (rewire-benchmark-data issue #226, second item) by a different agent from the extractor, against the extraction frozen at batch.jsonl SHA-256 d00df69afbdb0e148e158a51f8f9cb6dfe8903b590baf68a8d10bf6dc5ea5e5d, 13 records: 5 sources and 8 claims, no evaluations and no results. The reviewed batch holds 15 records, the two added ones being the metadata-correction claims this review wrote. No vocabulary concept is added and data/vocab is untouched; vocab-proposal.ttl proposes optical-character-recognition as a review method for the coordinator. All five artifacts were re-retrieved at 2026-11-16T00:48Z to 00:49Z: the Extended Data Table 1 page, the Extended Data Table 1 image, the Figure 2 page and the Supplementary Information PDF each reproduced their pinned SHA-256 byte for byte, and the nature.com article page did not, which is the behaviour its own hash_scope records and is corroborated by the other four from the same hosts matching in the same minute. The batch's central question is whether the peer-reviewed version prints different numbers from the stored bioRxiv v2 values, and its declared weakness was that the extractor's reading of the published ablation table was made by eye with the stored values in view. The review removed that weakness. The published Extended Data Table 1 is a 1594 by 949 raster JPEG with no text layer and tesseract is not installed, but macOS ships the Vision framework and swiftc is present, so the review built review/ocr.swift around VNRecognizeTextRequest (recognitionLevel accurate, usesLanguageCorrection false) and ran it over the re-downloaded JPEG at native size and at 2x. Each pass returned 136 numeric observations, every one at confidence 1.000, and the two passes agree on every value; the only difference anywhere is the column header read as ClinVar at 1x and Clin Var at 2x. review/grid.py rebuilt the 17 by 8 grid from the observation geometry alone, banding on vertical centre and ordering on horizontal centre, with no stored value in the script, and the reading was written to review/reviewer-reading-extended-data-table-1.tsv before any comparison was made. review/threeway.py then diffed that reading against each stored record's printed_value and numeric_value and against both value columns of the extractor's extract/comparison.tsv, rebuilding the row and column mapping from the OCR labels rather than trusting the extractor's: 136 cells checked three ways, 0 disagreements (review/threeway-result.txt). Coverage was recounted independently: 138 stored results cite gfm-guides-20261014-gpnmsa-source-biorxiv-v2, all 138 appear in comparison.tsv, and comparison.tsv holds nothing that does not cite that source, so the batch's 136 of 138 compared is exact. Because the stored values came from a pdftotext -layout parse of the preprint PDF and the reviewer's came from OCR of a publisher raster, two unrelated readings of two separately typeset artifacts agree on all 136 cells to the decimal place. The paywall was rechecked from scratch rather than accepted: the refetched article page carries the abstract then 'This is a preview of subscription content' with no Main or Methods section; Europe PMC returns PMID 39747647 with isOpenAccess N, inPMC N, hasPDF N and 'Subscription required'; Unpaywall reports oa_status green with two locations, both submittedVersion (bioRxiv and PMC10592768, the NIH preprint pilot copy); OpenAlex agrees; and the string TADBP occurs in no retrieved published artifact except the ProteinGym dataset list in Supplementary Table 3, with no AUROC beside it. The two stored DMS TADBP AUROCs therefore genuinely cannot be compared. The reviewer also re-downloaded the preprint and regenerated its text layer to check the batch's statements about it rather than take them on trust, confirming the preprint Figure 2 lettering (a to g, gnomAD at f), the preprint Supplementary Table 4 caption's pointers to Figure 2a, 2b, 2c and 2d, the six preprint supplementary table titles against the six published ones, and all 16 held-out accuracy cells of Supplementary Tables 1 and 2 as identical between the versions. Every claim was upheld. One claim's value was reworded, gpn-msa-published-20261116-claim-ablation-values-unchanged, so that it states how each of the two readings was produced and that the published Methods were not retrieved, rather than asserting sameness flatly. Two stored records were changed and recorded with npm run records -- change against docs/reviews/2026-11-16-gpn-msa-published.md: gfm-guides-20261014-gpnmsa-source-biorxiv-v2 had limitation 1 replaced (it said the published table was not read and the values might differ, which is now answered and would otherwise invite doubt about 136 checked results), limitation 4 extended to cite the published caption that settles the preprint caption's wrong panel pointers, a limitation added naming both numbering shifts, and a companion_of edge added to the published source record; and gfm-guides-20261014-gpnmsa-protocol-ablation-gnomad-odds-ratio had its source_locator amended to name both the preprint's Figure 2 panel (f) and the published version's panel (g). Every stored GPN-MSA locator was scanned for dependence on a Figure 2 panel letter of this paper and that protocol record is the only one affected; gfm-guides-20261014-gpnmsa-model-gpn-msa cites 'preprint v2 Figure 2a', which is version-qualified and does not move. The 228 stored locators naming 'Supplementary Table 4' were deliberately not rewritten: each is correct against the preprint it cites, so there is no error to correct, and the version hazard is recorded once on the source record instead of in 228 re-pinned records. No stored printed_value, numeric_value, metric, unit, direction, denominator or uncertainty was touched anywhere.
limitations: Automated review by a Claude (Opus 5) agent, independent of the extractor but not human scientific review. Nothing was reproduced: no model was run and no score recomputed. Reading printed numbers is not reproduction.

The published values rest on optical character recognition of a raster image. That is a machine reading and independent of both the extractor and the stored records, and it was corroborated by a second pass at a different scale and by agreement with a separate pdftotext channel, but OCR is a recognition step rather than a parse of a text layer. No deterministic route to these values exists while the publisher ships the table as a picture.

The store has no review-method concept for OCR. The records use the nearest existing concepts (independent-cell-check, rendered-source-visual-check, source-hash-verification) and name the technique in full in every method_note. vocab-proposal.ttl proposes optical-character-recognition.

The peer-reviewed Results and Methods body was not retrieved; it is paywalled at nature.com and in no open index. The two stored DMS TADBP AUROCs (GPN-MSA 0.83, ESM-1b 0.75) are therefore uncompared: 136 of 138, not 138 of 138.

Because the Methods were not retrieved, the published ablation definitions were not read. The caption says 'Ablations are detailed in Methods'. Identical values are evidence the settings did not change, not proof.

The nature.com article page does not reproduce its pinned hash and cannot: it varies advertising and session markup between retrievals. Its hash describes one retrieval, the record says so, and the passages the batch uses were confirmed verbatim in the reviewer's own copy instead.

npm run batch -- check-values was not run and no value-check.tsv exists. The batch contributes no result records, and its one values table is an image with no text layer, so the tool has nothing to parse. review/threeway.py is the comparison this batch has in its place.

The main comparisons against CADD, phyloP, phastCons, ESM-1b, Nucleotide Transformer, HyenaDNA, Enformer and SpliceAI are printed only as figures in both versions, with no Source Data file, and stay unextracted.

The three denominator claims for ClinVar, COSMIC and OMIM were not moved onto the dataset records, which keep missing_metadata.denominator with reason unreported. The counts come from a Figure 2 caption describing the main comparison, and Extended Data Table 1 says only that the ablation uses the same setting; for gnomAD the two sets are demonstrably different, since the ablation subsets the rare variants. The claims hold the evidence and the move is left to whoever owns the dataset records.

Published Figure 2 panel d gives 21,275 ClinVar pathogenic variants where panel c gives 21,273. The paper does not explain the difference. Panel d has no stored counterpart, so nothing depends on it; it is recorded as a lead.

The stored preprint source gfm-guides-20261014-gpnmsa-source-biorxiv-v2 has no reproducible byte check and cannot be given one. Three downloads taken during this review are all 2,247,726 bytes and gave two distinct hashes, neither of them the pinned 10411077df1ae59614f9a9a9f85384103d54127ba67a9b3c469a4a2d6c33cee4, so bioRxiv rotates between variants rather than stamping each request. The pin was not changed and no copy was archived: see ruling 5 in the dated review. The reproducible artifact is the pdftotext -layout text layer, byte-identical across all three downloads at c6e95eb807550bb97aa2b8991c013f28fe11742006582c25818fcf90cad30c79, which the source record's hash_scope asserts in prose without naming. Recording that hash is recommended and is left to whoever sequences cross-batch GPN-MSA record fixes.
